title: Genes Pass On, Scars Do Not

scenes.visual: Two cuttings from one hydrangea bush are planted in two gardens; one blooms blue, the other pink; same-genes chip; question mark; essential question appears.
scenes.tts: Take two cuttings from one hydrangea bush. Plant them in two gardens. When they bloom, one can be blue and the other pink. The two cuttings have the same genes. So where does the difference come from? Are all my traits from my genes, or do some come from how I live?
scenes.narration: Take two cuttings from one hydrangea bush. Plant them in two gardens. When they bloom, one can be blue and the other pink. The two cuttings have the same genes. So where does the difference come from? Are all my traits from my genes, or do some come from how I live?

scenes.visual: Two columns: inherited trait (parent to offspring along a genes arrow, eye color) and acquired trait (a living thing, during its life: scar, dyed hair, muscles built by exercise).
scenes.tts: Some traits are inherited. An inherited trait is passed from parents to offspring through genes. Eye color is one. Other traits are acquired. An acquired trait is a characteristic a living thing gets during its life. A scar is one. So are dyed hair, and muscles built by exercise.
scenes.narration: Some traits are inherited. An inherited trait is passed from parents to offspring through genes. Eye color is one. Other traits are acquired. An acquired trait is a characteristic a living thing gets during its life. A scar is one. So are dyed hair, and muscles built by exercise.

scenes.visual: A parent outline with skin cells, muscle cells and sex cells holding genes; scar and exercise change the skin and muscle cells only; only genes travel to the offspring, the scar stops.
scenes.tts: Why can't a scar be passed on? A new animal grows from sex cells. Sex cells carry the parent's genes. A scar changes skin cells. Lifting weights changes muscle cells. Neither changes the genes in the sex cells. So neither reaches the offspring.

scenes.visual: A living thing inside a dashed environment outline; soil, light, water, food, temperature arrive; then genes plus environment give many traits.
scenes.tts: Genes are not the whole story. The environment is everything around a living thing that can affect it. Soil, light, water, food and temperature are all part of it. Many traits depend on genes and the environment together.

scenes.visual: Soil to roots to flowers: aluminum moves in acidic soil and the flower turns blue; less acidic soil, pink; a soil pH bar with blue, in-between and pink zones.
scenes.tts: Back to the hydrangea. In many bigleaf hydrangeas, acidic soil lets the roots take up more aluminum. The aluminum helps make the flowers blue. In less acidic soil, the flowers are pink. Gardeners measure this with soil P H. A lower number means more acidic soil. About five to five point five gives blue. In between, the color is in between. Above about six to six point five gives pink.

scenes.visual: No: genes allow blue or pink and the soil picks; height from many genes plus food and health; genes can be inherited, scar, dyed hair, learned skill are not passed on.
scenes.tts: So, are all my traits from my genes? No. In many hydrangeas, the genes set which colors are possible. The soil helps decide which one appears. Your height works this way too. It depends on many genes, and on food and health while you grow. Traits coded in genes can be inherited. A scar, dyed hair or a learned skill cannot be passed to offspring.
